on, believed a device was streaming and set the TV's controllers aside with
nobody playing. A newly started Sunshine now starts from "nobody streaming".

**Pausing from a phone.** Holding Select did not open the menu in a PS3
game. Recorded on the A9: Sunshine lets go of Select and presses Home in the
same instant, and the path for emulators that run as programs of their own
read Select's release with Home already down, then counted Home's own press
as a second button (a shortcut, not a tap). Built-in games read the buttons
per frame and never saw it. Fixed for every pad: the shortcut button's own
press is not a second button. And with in-game shortcuts off (the default)
Home opens nothing anywhere, which left a phone on touch controls no way to
pause; **a streaming device's Home now always opens the menu**, every system
(MMagTech, 2026-10-08). **Sunshine's priority:** it keeps its capabilities on
one or two threads and drops them elsewhere, so the sound and video threads'
requests for priority were refused on every stream; `LimitNICE=-15` in the
unit lets any of its threads go that far.

**Found on the way.** The pause menu closed itself when a pad came back
(it left with Home held, being switched off); fixed for every pad. Steam's
session picks 4K 120 Hz HDR on the LG C1 and the TV stays black: #290.
#289 (a pad back mid-game ignored by PS2) did not reproduce; its one
unrepeated condition, the phone's pad as player 2, cannot arise now that a
stream's pads are seated apart.

### 40. Controller battery on the top bar, issue #293

**Decided with MMagTech, 2026-10-08, from his proposal on #293 ("nothing in
here is set in stone") and measurements on the A9; judged on the TV through
the loop.** SETTINGS.md, Controllers, has what the screen does; this is why,
and what changed from the proposal.

**Measured first, every paired pad (journal and sysfs, A9, 2026-10-08):**

| Pad | Kernel (power_supply) | SDL 3.4.16 |
|---|---|---|
| Xbox One S, Bluetooth | 52%, Discharging | unknown for 20 minutes (its own HIDAPI driver, 10/40/70/100 steps, charging only on USB) |
| 8BitDo Lite 2, Switch mode | level (Normal, then High), Charging on a charger within 5 s | unknown (hid-nintendo has it; SDL steps aside) |
| 8BitDo Lite 2, its own mode (2dc8:5112) | nothing (hid-generic) | nothing (not in SDL's 8BitDo driver) |
| Wii Remotes, through the bridge | nothing (the bridge hides them) | not SDL's |
| Sunshine's stand-in pad | 100%, Discharging, always (the real pad's light was amber) | |

So **the kernel first, as the proposal said**; SDL only for a pad the kernel
has nothing for (my note on the issue had it the other way round, from
reading SDL's API rather than its Linux source, which has no battery code
for pads the kernel drives). **Read on a worker thread, woken by the
kernel's own uevents, not polled** (reading a HID battery's capacity can ask
the pad over the air). **A stream's pad is always label only.** **Wii
Remotes: the console app reads them itself on Home** (wiiremote.cpp already
asked each for its status on connect); it asks again once a minute while
one is on and out of a game. No bridge change: in a game Dolphin has them.

**Four segments, one rule per kind of reading.** A percentage: above 75, 50,
25; sticky 3% at each line so 50-51% does not flicker. A level: Full 4, High
3, Normal 2, Low and Critical 1. A Wii Remote's byte on the Wii's own scale
(RVL SDK `__a1_20_status_report`, from the Super Mario Galaxy decompilation):
0x55 4, 0x44 3, 0x33 2, else 1. The alkalines in his Remotes read 112, full
on a Wii. **The warning is the last segment for every pad**, not "10%":
some pads step 100/75/50/25/0 and never report 10 (MMagTech caught it).
Amber as a warning stage was dropped for that reason; then **colour came
back on the fill only** ("a little color would be beneficial"): green 3-4,
amber 2, red 1, outline and labels grey.

**Changed from the proposal, with MMagTech:**
- **On every screen with the top bar, not Home only** (Home, Library,
  Search, Settings): the bar keeps its shape as you move along it. Never in
  a game or on a game's page.
- **The notice only where the bar is not**: in a game and on a game's page.
  The console's one notice style ("P2 battery low", the problem dot), not
  the RetroAchievements card (it has existed since #74, 2026-10-06; my note
  said otherwise): both were shown over Tetris, and the card needed a second
  line and covered the game's NEXT box.
- **Wii Remotes as W1-W4**, the light on the Remote: out of a game their
  numbers are their own, so a P would have made two P1s. Their notice would
  only ever have fired out of a game, so they warn in the row only.
- **A battery outline, not rising bars** (bars read as phone signal), at the
  name's size: a step down was tried and did not look right beside the name.
- **Fade and slide** when pads come and go; laid out at once when the bar
  comes back from a game, and an account switch happens under the curtain.
- **The name gives way** (shortened) rather than the row running into
  Settings. Eight controllers, Offline and a download at once still overlap;
  judged not worth more.
- **Streaming:** the row follows the console's player list, so a stream
  shows its own pads (label only) and the TV's pads and Remotes leave it. For
  about half a second after a stream starts the TV's row still shows, until
  Sunshine's log says a client connected; left as is (MMagTech: not worth
  custom scripting).
- **No wiki page**: the console's docs are in the repository (SETTINGS.md).

**Also fixed:** re-pairing a pad the console knows but that was paired to
something else since (bluez: AlreadyExists) failed with "Couldn't pair" and
no way out on screen; it now forgets the old pairing and pairs again. **Found
on the way:** a stream started while the screen is asleep stays black, #294.

### 41. The diagnostic report, issue #195

**Decided with MMagTech, 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-10, on #195; built on the
`diagnostic-report` branch.** The goal, his words: a report a person can
share on GitHub, that contains nothing sensitive once shared, and that is
enough on its own to troubleshoot the issue from. He forwards community
reports to the assistant, so what goes in is the assistant's call; his checks
are the screen and privacy.

**One tool, two ways in.** `/usr/libexec/cabinetos-report` (Python; also
`cabinetos-report` on the path) gathers and scrubs; the frontend only runs
it. So Developer access makes the same file, and a console whose frontend
will not start can still make one. About 3 seconds and 1 to 1.5 MB on the A9.

**By part of the system, not by chosen facts**, so the next kind of fault is
covered: a summary, every setting, then the machine (firmware names, BIOS,
processor and AVX, PCI and USB devices with drivers, firmware loads),
graphics, the screen (EDID decoded, modes), drives and space (including what
nothing cleans up, and Mesa's shader cache against its 1 GB cap), controllers
and Bluetooth, network and Tailscale, Remote Play, Steam, updates, the server,
File access and Developer access, services, the games of the two boots,
every emulator's last log, and **the system log of this boot and the one
before** (routine audit lines and SSH logins left out, SELinux refusals and
SSH failures kept; a boot over 5 MB keeps its first 1 MB and last 4 MB and
says so). The Remote Play faults #294 and #296 are why: a list of facts had
nothing of Sunshine in it.

**Private details are replaced before anything is written, in two layers.**
First every value the console knows (server address, profile and
RetroAchievements names, tokens, Wi-Fi and connection names, Tailscale names
and addresses, Remote Play device names, Bluetooth names that are not
controllers, serial numbers of drives, USB devices and the screen, a changed
hostname, Steam names), then patterns for what no list knows (email, IPv4 and
IPv6 addresses, MAC and Bluetooth addresses keeping the maker's half, serial
numbers, `ts.net` names, Steam IDs, secrets in key=value form). One pass over
the text, so a placeholder is never replaced inside another; each value keeps
one placeholder throughout. **It fails closed**: a known value found after the
scrub means nothing is written. Measured on the A9 before it existed:
Tailscale writes the account email into the log, and save paths carry
profile names. **Game titles stay.** Left out on purpose: the PIN (four digits
replaced everywhere would point at it), the EDID hex dump (raw serial bytes),
and Tailscale's nearest relays (together they say roughly where the house is).
The project's own public names (`ghcr.io/mmagtech/cabinetos`) are never
replaced, even when a profile shares the name.

**How it leaves the console: the QR code is a download link** (MMagTech,
2026-09-30). While the screen is open the console serves that one file at
`http://<home network address>:<port>/<8 random characters>`, bound to the
home network address only (not Tailscale), on a port the firewall's home zone
already allows; closing the screen stops it. Sent as an attachment, because
an iPhone shows plain text in the browser instead of saving it. The file is
also in File access, `reports/`, the last five kept. No PIN on the row: it
changes nothing and nothing private is in the file.

**Checked against real faults of this project, 2026-10-10** (would the
report alone have pointed at the cause?):

| Fault | What in the report shows it |
|---|---|
| A stream started while the screen is asleep stays black (#294) | Sunshine's lines and the frontend's `[idle]` and `[remoteplay]` lines in the system log |
| Steam over Moonlight: black picture, sound plays (#296) | Steam's state, the handover and Sunshine's lines in the log |
| The boot on software rendering | `GL_RENDERER` (llvmpipe) in the summary, the session's gamescope attempts, the kernel's firmware lines |
| A PS2 save that did not reach the server | `[save]` and `[sync]` lines, and whether the server answered |
| A pad that pairs once and never reconnects | `Trusted: no` in its Bluetooth entry |
| A game that draws nothing, a black screen with sound | the `[core]` and `[launch]` lines of the game |
| An emulator that closes (RPCS3, Xenia, Eden) | `[standalone] ... ended after` and the emulator's own last log |
| No Wi-Fi or GPU on a new machine | PCI devices with no driver in use, and the firmware the kernel asked for |
| A drive that is not used | its filesystem in the drive list and the `[drives]` reason |
| An update that failed | `rpm-ostree status`, the update status file, and bootc's lines |

Not reachable from a report: what only the screen shows, the phone's side of
Remote Play, and when it happened. The issue template asks for those. The
installer is a different system (no report there).

**Not built, #315 (after first release):** a report from a console with no
network. That console is almost always a new machine stuck at first run's
network step, which has no skip, so the report would have to be offered
there and written to a drive a PC can read (FAT32 for the report only; ext4,
which the console's own Format makes, is unreadable on Windows and Mac).

**Logs do not fill the drive:** journald caps itself at 4 GB (less on a
small drive, and keeps 15% free); the A9's was 1.4 GB after three weeks and
about ninety boots. Emulator logs are one file each, replaced every run
(260 KB in all); reports keep five.

### 42. How to, in About, issue #314

**Decided with MMagTech on the TV, 2026-10-10.** SETTINGS.md, About, has
what it shows; this is why.

- **What is on it** is what somebody at the TV gets stuck on with a pad in
  hand: leaving a game, the pause menu (three ways), shortcuts, menus,
  switching person, Steam (it is only in the Power menu, and the way back is
  Steam's own "Switch to Desktop"), pairing (a Bluetooth pad, a Wii Remote's
  red sync button), ejecting a drive. Left off: what the console says where
  it matters (a drive it cannot use, Format's ext4), and what is found by
  using it (favourites, save states).
- **Shortcuts are always shown**, greyed while off with where to turn them
  on: hidden, nobody learns they exist (MMagTech).
- **Settings' shape, not a page.** One page of headings and lines was built
  first: "it kind of looks hideous". The sections as Settings' categories
  look like the rest of the console.
- **The wiki's code carries the cabinet.** The address never changes, so the
  code is made once by `tools/make-wiki-qr.py` (segno, level H) and stored
  as data; the console's own encoder, used for pairing, Tailscale and the
  diagnostic report, is untouched. The tile is 14% of the code: grown in
  steps and decoded by OpenCV's two readers at TV-photo sizes, 7, 10 and 14%
  read as well as a plain level-H code, 19% lost a reader at two sizes, 24%
  read at none. A plain level-H code is denser than level M's (37 modules
  against 29) and both fail under about 140 px in the photo; the code is
  half the screen's height on any TV, so that is a 32-inch screen from
  across a room. The address is a row above it, to type instead.
- **With it: Controllers became one row** opening a panel (three pads filled
  the page), and **Developer access moved last in About** (the everyday rows
  never move when it shows; it still appears in view).

### 43. Games on several discs, issue #162

**The plan is on #162 (agreed with MMagTech 2026-10-10/11); this records what
was decided while building it, from the disc rig's measurements on the A9
(2026-10-11, branch `multi-disc`, comments on #162).** `frontend/src/disc.h`
holds the rules.

- **Only multi-disc games show anything:** one pause-menu row, *Change disc:
  Disc 1 of 4*, after Screenshot and beside Look (the one-press rows stay
  together, the two *Name: value* rows sit side by side; MMagTech on the TV,
  2026-10-11), and *Disc N of M* on the game page. Everything else is the
  question panel: every disc, the one in the drive marked *In the drive*,
  focus on the next; then **Insert** / **Insert and restart**. The panel
  replaces the pause menu while it is up (the menu's words showed through its
  glass). One thing to do is said, not focused: *Press (A) to insert and
  restart* (3DO, and the disc already in).
- **The words are what a person does with a real console** (MMagTech,
  2026-10-11): swap the disc, or swap it and press Reset. The first wording,
  *Insert it* / *Start over on it*, never said the disc goes in, so the Soviet
  disc of Red Alert read as an Insert. A panel row acts on its disc's own
  number, not its place in the list.
- **Saturn keeps both choices** (MMagTech, 2026-10-11). Its lid always resets
  to the BIOS, so the two converge (Insert passes through the CD player
  screen, Insert and restart skips it); one action was considered and set
  aside because no survey can rule out a Saturn game that swaps mid-play.
- **Disc numbers are the names' own** when every name numbers its disc from 1,
  so a disc missing on RomM leaves its gap (*Disc 1 of 4 · Disc 2 missing*,
  the panel lists 1, 3, 4); otherwise the place in the order.
- **Start over, per system, measured:** PS1 and Dreamcast take the core's own
  start disc (`set_initial_image`), now stated on every launch, disc 1
  included, because Flycast keeps the last one it was told. Saturn: both ways
  were tried with Panzer Dragoon Saga (disc N put in before the first frame,
  and the list written with disc N first); both boot disc N's title, and
  states loaded across both list orders. **Kept: before the first frame**, so
  Beetle Saturn's disc 0 is always disc 1. Sega CD and GameCube: the list
  with disc N first. 3DO: the disc's own file.
- **Saturn's lid reset is real and needs a press:** Insert drops the game to
  the BIOS CD player, which waits on *Start Application*; Start boots the new
  disc. Panzer Dragoon Saga asks for exactly this ("Press the CD Door Button
  to enter the Saturn Bios Screen"), and its save continues on disc 2.
- **GameCube: no menu, no remembered disc, no Disc N of M.** Dolphin's
  libretro port (1a0f972) never moves its disc index for its own
  AutoDiscChange and never clears its disc list, so nothing outside Dolphin
  can know which disc is in. The list always starts at disc 1; the game asks
  for the disc it needs. `AutoDiscChange = True` is in the Dolphin.ini the
  console writes.
- **Before any game unloads, the drive goes back to the list's first entry**
  (lid open, index 0, lid closed). Flycast (a172e00) keeps its disc index
  across games and `read_m3u` reads nothing unless it is 0, so after a change
  to disc 2 every later Dreamcast launch was refused until the app restarted.
  A fallback on our side; the upstream report waits on MMagTech's go.
- **DECIDED (c), 2026-10-11: achievements are not told about a disc change**
  (the plan's item 10). Softcore only on this console; hardcore stays off for
  what it costs to maintain under RetroAchievements' rules. If hardcore is
  ever wanted, (a) is the work. The question as it was: rcheevos' `rc_client_begin_change_media` takes the
  new disc's hash; it only re-checks that the disc belongs to the game and, in
  hardcore (off on this console), turns hardcore off for an unknown one.
  RomM gives one hash per game and the console reads no disc. The options:
  (a) hash each disc on the console (rcheevos' own disc hashing, which needs
  a CHD reader built in); (b) pass the game's hash again, which tells
  rcheevos nothing; (c) leave it, since unlocks do not depend on it in
  softcore.
- **States carry their disc in their name,** `Game (Disc 2) [time].state`, so a
  state from any device brings its disc; the disc goes in before the state
  loads. Only pcsx_rearmed restores it by itself. Measured on PS1, Saturn,
  Sega CD and Dreamcast (a Skies of Arcadia disc 2 state loaded with disc 1 in
  comes back on disc 2). **3DO refuses another disc's state** (*That state is
  on Disc 3*): Opera has no drive, so nothing could put that disc in; a state
  picked on the game page starts the game on its disc. GameCube has no states.
- **Flycast sometimes will not save a state** (it refused at frame 4000 of a
  boot and saved at 5200, on either disc), and the console then says *No save
  states for this system*, which is wrong for that moment. Not a disc issue.
- **Known, not fixed:** a disc the game is not asking for can crash PS1's core
  (Lightrec) and with it the app; on hardware the game would hang. Insert at
  the game's own prompt passes on PS1, Saturn, Dreamcast and Sega CD (on the
  TV, 2026-10-11, with downloaded saves; #162). The wiki says to insert only
  when the game asks.
- **Upstream and the cores' own habits** (#162, 2026-10-11): Flycast's
  `disk_index` is reported (flyinghead/flycast#2541) and our drive-back-to-
  disc-1 before unload stays until a fixed Flycast is pinned; the lid must be
  closed again there, because Flycast also keeps the lid (a lid left open
  started the next game open). Genesis Plus GX never closes the `.m3u` it
  reads, and PCSX ReARMed keeps the last game's disc open until the next PS1
  game: a few files held until the app restarts. Dolphin's disk-control list
  grows by each launch's discs, but it boots and auto-changes from that
  launch's own `.m3u`, so the next GameCube game is unaffected (measured: RE4
  twice, then Ikaruga).

### 44. Volume keys, issue #351

**Decided with MMagTech, 2026-10-11, on #351; built and tested on the A9 the
same night.** Reported from a Steam Deck: the rocker did nothing, and the
console had no volume control at all. A TV console's volume is the
television's, which is why there was none; the rocker sends the standard keys
(`KEY_VOLUMEUP`/`KEY_VOLUMEDOWN`, 115/114, from the Deck's built-in "AT
Translated Set 2 keyboard") and nothing listened.

**The rules (`frontend/src/volume.{h,cpp}`, walked by `--volume-test`):**
- **Volume keys from any keyboard step the system volume** (the default sound
  output, `wpctl`, 5% a press, never above 100%), **silently**: no bar, as
  with the television's own volume.
- **Read from the kernel's key devices, not the window**, so they work while
  a separate emulator (PS2, PS3, Switch, Xbox, Xbox 360, Wii U) has the
  screen. Read only, never grabbed. Keyboards are the `input` group's alone
  by default (the console's user could read only its pads), so
  `71-cabinetos-key-devices.rules` gives the seat's user read access to
  every key device, as systemd does for pads. Only a device whose sysfs key
  list has a volume key is opened.
- **At every start the volume goes back to full, unless the machine has a
  built-in screen** (a DRM connector of type eDP, DSI or LVDS, Linux's
  internal panels). A keyboard can never leave a TV console quiet with no way
  back for a controller; a handheld keeps its level. **Measured:** a session
  start remakes the TV's sound output (node 65, then 70, then 55 within a
  second), and the last comes back at WirePlumber's saved level; once, after
  a PS2 game, that finished after the console's reset and left 0.95. So for
  30 s after start a level that is not full is set again, unless a volume key
  has been used.
- **The diagnostic report lists every keyboard**, whether it has the volume
  keys, its named special keys and every key code, plus the volume now and
  whether there is a built-in screen. A handheld's report answers this in one
  line.

**Tested on the A9 by injected keys (ydotool), reading the sink back:** Home,
Snes9x (in the console), PS2 (Burnout 3), PS3 (RPCS3, its own process) and
Switch (Eden, a Flatpak): each press 5% in each, nothing drawn. Full at each
start. Whether a given handheld's buttons send these keys is its owner's to
confirm; the Deck's do, by its kernel log and an owner's evtest.

### 45. Smart collections, issue #352

**Decided with MMagTech, 2026-10-12, on #352 and at the TV.** Reported on
RomM 5.4.0: about twenty smart collections showed on RomM's page and none on
the console, which asked only `/api/collections`.

- **Smart collections show with the regular ones**, from
  `/api/collections/smart`, which the reference RomM (5.3.1) also serves. A
  server without the route (404) has none. Opening one asks
  `/api/roms?smart_collection_id=N`, so the server works out the members at
  that moment.
- **RomM's autogenerated collections stay out** (`/api/collections/virtual`,
  115 franchise and genre groups on the reference server): they bury the
  collections people made, which is why RomM's own setting to show them is
  off there.
- **Who sees which is RomM's answer, per account.** Both lists hold the
  caller's own collections and every public one (`for_user` in RomM 5.3.1),
  and the console loads each account's library with that account's token, an
  account switch included. **The family case is the test:** a public
  collection a parent makes ("games the kids can play") shows on a child's
  account; the parent's private ones do not. Offline shows no collections.
- **The order: the person's own first, then each other person's shared ones
  under "From <name>".** Own: their Favorites first, then A to Z, regular and
  smart together (how a collection was made is not what it is for). Then one
  group per other account with something public, people A to Z by RomM
  username, each A to Z; a group starts a new row, and the heading is a label
  that focus never lands on. Every account on the server counts, not only
  those paired on the console. Tabs by kind (regular, smart) were rejected:
  an extra press and a choice every time, for short lists. **Judged on the
  TV** with a stand-in for five people (`tools/romm-readonly-relay.py ...
  people`); if a household that shares a lot finds it long, the next step is
  one sideways row per person, like Home's shelves (MMagTech: "maybe even
  permanently" as it is).
- **L2 and R2 jump person to person** in Collections, as they jump letter to
  letter in a game grid (MMagTech's idea); back from inside a group goes to
  its start first. One jump a pull.
- **A Favorites is personal.** Another account's Favorites never shows, even
  public: a parent's public Favorites showed on a child's account as a
  second "Favorites" tile. A favourite goes to the person's own Favorites,
  and the one the console makes is named "Favorites", as RomM's page names
  it (it said "Favourites" until now; one made before keeps that name).
- **A tile is its query, not its id.** RomM counts platforms, collections and
  smart collections separately, all from 1, and the Library told tiles apart
  by id alone: a collection's corrected count ("4 of 12") could land on the
  platform with the same id, and a big grid's later pages could fill the
  wrong tile. Each tile now carries the query that lists its games
  (`platform_ids=5`, `collection_id=2`, `smart_collection_id=2`).
- **Left as RomM does, on purpose:** a public smart collection whose filter
  depends on the person (has saves, favourites, played) shows the owner's
  count on its tile but opens on the viewer's games, because RomM stores the
  members for the owner and works them out for whoever opens it. Rare, and
  RomM's page does the same; MMagTech: too many scenarios to account for.

**Tested on the A9 through the loop, 2026-10-12**, with test collections on
MMagTech's account: signed in as the second account, only his public ones
showed, under "From MMagTech", with the second account's own Favorites
first; back on his account, all of his showed in one A to Z list, Favorites
first. Another account's public Favorites staying hidden was shown with the
stand-in (Sam's), not with his own: his was private again by the time that
rule was built. A favourite pressed on the
second account while his Favorites was public reached RomM and left his 34
games unchanged. SHMUP (collection 2) and `Test: Racing` (smart collection 2)
each opened their own games and kept their own count lines.

### 46. Where the sound goes, issue #341

**Decided by MMagTech, 2026-10-13; built and tested on the A9 2026-10-14.**
deletableman's HCAR5000-MI (sold as AM06 Pro) played into an empty jack: its
jack is a built-in C-Media USB chip that cannot sense a plug, and WirePlumber
ranks an analog output above HDMI, so the chip won.

**The rule:** the TV the picture is on first; a headphone jack that senses
the plug takes over while headphones are in and hands back when they come
out; nothing else takes the sound from the TV (not a jack that cannot sense,
not USB sound, not Bluetooth for now); no setting. Bluetooth audio, if it
comes, is one more kind of output in the "takes over" list.

**Built with WirePlumber's own settings only**
(`system_files/usr/share/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/60-cabinetos-sound-output.conf`),
as its documentation describes (*Node priorities*): USB sound outputs get
`priority.session` 100, below any HDMI (696 on the A9), and
`node.restore-default-targets` is off. A jack that senses the plug needs no
rule: WirePlumber switches its card off while nothing is plugged in, so the
output only exists while headphones are in, and its own rank (1009 on the
A9) is above HDMI. A small WirePlumber script that ignores any output unable
to sense a plug was considered and rejected: more than standard settings,
for hardware the rule says not to account for. **Both held only on a sound
chip with no built-in speaker, as the A9's has none. Built-in speakers are
handled since 2026-10-22 by one edit to a PipeWire file, not a script (#547,
below).**

**Why the memory goes off.** A chosen output beats every priority, and
WirePlumber kept the choice across restarts. On the A9 the TV was chosen, so
headphones never took over (baseline, 2026-10-13: jack sensed, headphone
output switched on, sound stayed on the TV in every step). The choice was
Sunshine's: it sets the default by name at the end of every stream.

**Measured on the A9, 2026-10-14** (`wpctl`, the jack's `Headphone Jack`
control and the app's link, once a second): AirPods Max over USB-C ranked
1109 by WirePlumber and 100 with the rule, and the TV kept the sound; the
3.5 mm headphones took the sound within a second of going in, in Home, an
arcade game and a PS3 game (RPCS3), and every unplug brought it back to the
TV; TV standby and back, TV; a Remote Play stream carried the sound to the
phone. Every separate emulator plays to the system default (Eden `auto`,
RPCS3 and xemu their built-in default, Xenia SDL's, Cemu `default`), so the
rule covers them without touching any.

**Known gap, waiting on Sunshine (#390):** after a Remote Play session,
headphones do not take over until the console restarts, because Sunshine's
end-of-stream choice holds for the rest of the run. Unplugging still always
returns the sound to the TV.

**Open:** the volume goes back to full at every start (#351 above), on the
default output. With headphones in at start, that is the headphones (#391, waiting, not built).

#### Built-in speakers (#547), 2026-10-21 and 22

**The fault.** A Beelink SER9 (#547, "Sounds plays only from onboard
speakers (Beelink ser9)") played everything through the speaker in its
case. Its ALC897 drives a built-in speaker (`speaker_outs=1` in the kernel
log), and a speaker has no plug to sense, so its connector reports
`unknown`. WirePlumber passes over an output only when its connector says
`no` (`lutils.haveAvailableRoutes`), so the speaker counted and its analog
rank beat the TV. The same fault is in the report on #416 ("PCSX2 loads the
wrong bios for the region of the game"): an HP EliteDesk 705 G4, its CX20632
with `speaker_outs=1`, the speaker chosen over an Acer CB272U whose EDID
declares speakers. Nobody there mentioned sound. The A9 never showed it:
its ALC269VC has only the headphone jack, which says `no` while empty. No
priority can fix it: the speaker and the headphone jack are one output
whose connector changes when headphones go in. The three HCAR5000-MI
reports (#341, #400, #529) already had the TV as the default.

**Decided by MMagTech, 2026-10-21 and 22.** A built-in speaker never takes
the sound from the TV. When the TV's sound is gone (the screen asleep, the TV
off or unplugged) the console is silent, never the speaker: a console is
designed around a TV, every modern TV has speakers, a monitor without them
has the jack, and Remote Play carries the sound through Sunshine's own
output. Falling back to the speaker was considered and rejected: the
screen's sleep removes the TV's output (#228, below), so the sound would move
to the speaker at every sleep and come back only if SDL noticed the TV's
return. No sound menu: picking an output would turn the headphone switching
off, its "Automatic" would still need this fix, and #341 said no setting.
Handheld PCs and laptops are not targets (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Made for a PC
attached to a TV", 2026-10-22): what this does to their built-in speakers
does not decide anything. He asked for the fix that is easiest to maintain,
and accepts a build that fails on an upstream change so long as it says so.

**Researched 2026-10-22** (three agents; GitLab issue pages were unreadable
to them). No setting in PipeWire or WirePlumber does this; WirePlumber's
documentation says routes of unknown availability count as usable "since
built-in speakers have no jack detection", and its issue #166, "Give HDMI
outputs a higher priority than internal speakers", exists (its answer was
not read). Bazzite does it per machine: the Framework Desktop's hardware
profile raises one HDMI node by name (`51-preferHDMI.conf`). Batocera and
Kodi give the player a menu. PulseAudio deliberately never switched to HDMI
by itself (`module-switch-on-connect` ignores "hdmi" by default). ChromeOS
ranks exactly this rule (headphones, line out, USB and Bluetooth 3, HDMI 2,
internal speaker 1, in `audio_device.cc`), because its sound daemon keeps
the speaker and the headphones apart. Ruled out: raising HDMI's priority
(headphones would never take over); a kernel `patch=` or hint (per codec,
and a wrong pin silences a machine); a copied profile set (a large file that
drifts); `api.acp.hidden-ports` (undocumented, and a card with only a
speaker would still win).

**Built:** `build_files/built-in-speaker.sh`, run by `build.sh`. In PipeWire's
`/usr/share/alsa-card-profile/mixer/paths/analog-output-speaker.conf` the
sections `[Jack Speaker Phantom]` and `[Jack Speaker Front Phantom]` change
`state.plugged` and `state.unplugged` from `unknown` to `no`. The kernel
gives a built-in speaker a phantom jack that always reads plugged in (since
2012, so that sound servers could see fixed speakers), and in PipeWire a
plugged-in jack that says `no` "should override all other availability
information" (`calc_port_state`, `spa/plugins/alsa/acp/acp.c`, read at
1.6.9, the image's version). So a built-in speaker counts as an empty
headphone jack does: the onboard analog output exists only while headphones
are in, which is how the A9 already behaves. The script fails the build if
either section does not read exactly as at 1.6.9, or the file is missing.
Cards set up by their own UCM profile never read this file: the image ships
one for the Steam Deck (`ucm2/AMD/acp5x`, Valve's Jupiter and Galileo), so a
Deck keeps its speakers. Not covered, and left as they were: a jack other
than a speaker that cannot sense a plug, and a speaker with no phantom jack.
A machine with no HDMI or DisplayPort sound at all is silent through a
built-in speaker. The diagnostic report's Sound section lists each card's
outputs and what each connector reads.

**First built as a WirePlumber script, 2026-10-21, and replaced.** A Lua hook
before `find-best-default-node` dropped every sound-card output that was not
HDMI and not sensed "yes". It worked in WirePlumber's own Lua against 14
stand-in setups and loaded in a real WirePlumber on the VM, but it leaned on
WirePlumber's hook names and needed care to load safely: listed as optional
in a profile it never loaded, required it would let a broken script stop all
sound, and loaded after the event source it missed the start-up choice. The
file edit has none of that.

**Tested 2026-10-22:** the rule above read in PipeWire 1.6.9's source; the
build step run on the A9 against a copy of the image's file (exactly the
four lines change; run again on the edited file, on a reworded section and
with the file missing, it stops the build); the Steam Deck's UCM profile
found on the image. **Not tested on a real built-in speaker:** the A9 has
none, so the reporter's update is the test.

#### Sound dying until a restart (#228): the 2026-10-18 failure, read from the A9's logs

**Read overnight 2026-10-18, read-only**: the journal of the failing boot
(`journalctl -b -2`), tonight's boot live, the PipeWire dump the finding
session kept, and SDL 3.4.18's source (the A9's `SDL3-3.4.18-1.fc44`, read
at the `release-3.4.18` tag). Nothing was changed or pressed on the console.
The case: no sound in Spyro: Year of the Dragon at about 4:27 PM on
2026.10.18.6, the app's stream linked to the TV and running, pw-top's ERR
for it rising 47 a second, silence recorded from the TV's output (#228's
comment of 2026-10-18).

**What the log shows (Eastern time).** The app started at 15:53:02
(`[sound] interface audio at 48000 Hz`) and sat on Home. 16:03:02 `[idle]
dim -> blank after 600s without input`, 16:03:03 `[idle] display asleep:
gamescope took it`. Nothing else touched PipeWire until the TV came back:
16:26:31 `drm: current connector 'HDMI-A-1' disconnected`, back at 16:26:32,
again at 16:26:37 and 16:26:38, then 16:26:44 `[idle] display awake:
gamescope took it`. Spyro opened its sound at 16:27:25 (`[frontend] audio
out at 44100 Hz`), and every ten-second line after it was normal (`[audio]
30` to `54 ms waiting to play`; `sound per game frame +0.00%`, which since
#398 reads -100.00% for a silent core, so the core made sound). PipeWire and
WirePlumber log nothing at their default level, and the kernel logged
nothing about sound after the probe at 15:52:57.

- **The misses began at the blank.** 77,319 at the first reading (about
  16:30 to 16:31; the dump is from 16:31) at 46.875 a second (48,000 /
  1024) is 27.5 minutes: about 16:03:00 to 16:03:30, the blank, not the
  TV's return.
- **The silent stream was the one opened at start-up, never replaced.** The
  dump of it (node 61) reads `object.serial` 61, `client.id` 60,
  `node.loop.name` `SDLAudioP15`, `target.object`
  `alsa_output.pci-0000_c6_00.1.hdmi-stereo`, driven by node 53. A serial
  equal to its id is an object made before PipeWire had reused any id, and
  tonight's boot starts the same way (the app's SDL device watcher is client
  59; ids 60 and 61 are free now).
- **Blanking the screen removes the TV's sound output.** Tonight's boot, read
  at 22:30 with the screen asleep since 21:03:58: ELD `monitor_present 0`,
  no HDMI sink, only `Dummy Output` (`auto_null`), the app's stream on it.
  Dummy Output is pipewire-pulse's (`module-always-sink`,
  `/usr/share/pipewire/pipewire-pulse.conf`), and pipewire-pulse runs only
  once something speaks Pulse to it: tonight an overnight ssh session
  started it at 21:04:26; in the failing boot it never ran
  (`pipewire-pulse.socket` listening at 15:53:01, no `Started
  pipewire-pulse.service`). **So from 16:03 to 16:26 the console had no
  sound output at all.**
- **Tonight SDL moved the app; on 2026-10-18 nothing moved it.** The app's
  stream now is a new one (node 65, serial 139, `SDLAudioP27`,
  `target.object` `auto_null`, ERR steady at 6): SDL replaced it when the
  default output became Dummy Output, 28 s after the blank.

**Why that is silence: SDL's "zombie" device.** When PipeWire removes a
sink, SDL marks its device disconnected and swaps in stand-in functions;
anything opened on the default output (both of the app's streams,
`SDL_AUDIO_DEVICE_DEFAULT_PLAYBACK` in `sound.cpp`, `startup.cpp` and
`launch.cpp`) is "left on the zombie device for later migration", and moves
only when PipeWire's `default.audio.sink` names a device SDL knows. With no
sink there is nothing to move to. SDL's PipeWire stream stays open:
WirePlumber relinks it (SDL leaves `node.dont-reconnect` unset; its
`target.object` names the HDMI sink), PipeWire calls it every cycle, and
SDL's callback mixes the app's sound into a scratch buffer and drops it (so
the game's queue drains at the right speed and the `[audio]` and `[pace]`
lines look normal) but never takes or hands back a PipeWire buffer
(`ZombieGetDeviceBuf`, `ZombiePlayDevice`), so PipeWire counts a miss every
cycle and plays silence. Spyro's stream, opened on the default at 16:27:25,
joined the zombie too (SDL "pretends to open" a zombie device). Every
reading of 2026-10-18 matches this, and a restart is a new process with a
new SDL, which is why it brings the sound back.

**Why the TV's return did not move it back: two candidates, not told
apart.**
1. **The returning sink reused the old one's PipeWire id.** SDL's PipeWire
   backend names each device by the node's id (`PW_ID_TO_HANDLE(id)`), and
   PipeWire gives a freed id to the next object; nothing else used PipeWire
   in those 23 minutes. The sink at 16:31 was id 53, and the start-up sink
   was very likely 53 too (assumed from tonight's boot, whose start-up
   layout is the same and whose id 53 is a reused one, between the MIDI
   ports and the camera device, beside four reused or free port ids). Two
   devices then share one handle while the zombie is still alive, and SDL's
   lookup of the new default (`SDL_FindPhysicalAudioDeviceByHandle`: first
   match in a hash table, zombies not skipped) can return the zombie itself,
   which is "already the default", so nothing moves. SDL asserts that
   handles are unique (`SDL_AddAudioDevice`); the same family is open
   upstream as libsdl-org/SDL#16133 ("SDL_audio.c assert in
   SDL_AddAudioDevice when PC returns from sleep"), moved by SDL's
   maintainer to 3.6.0.
2. **The default arrived before SDL knew the sink.** SDL adds a new sink
   only after a round trip to PipeWire (`hotplug_core_sync`) and looks the
   new default up by name among the sinks it has finished adding
   (`change_default_device`); a `default.audio.sink` that arrives first is
   dropped and never retried.

Both need the sink to vanish with no other output to fall back on, which is
why it takes a blank (or anything else that removes the sink: restarting
WirePlumber under the app gave the same 47 a second on 2026-10-14, testing
lessons) and why most wakes still have sound. Earlier boots blanked and
woke with no pipewire-pulse (00:40 to 07:06, then Battle Clash on snes9x at
07:12; 08:32 to 10:09) and no silence was reported; not checked by ear.

**Ruled out:** #280's chip power state (in force: `power_save_controller` N,
both controllers active, no `Refused to change power state`); the image
(2026.10.18.6 touches no sound code); volume and mute (1.00, not muted); the
core (it made sound, above); the silent day's starved sound thread (the
queue drained normally, so SDL's callback ran every cycle).

**Not known:** whether #228's first case (2026-10-02, silence after a
restart with the stream linked) was this too. A session start remakes the
TV's sink within a second (testing lessons, 2026-10-11), which can leave the
same zombie; no ERR was read that day.

**The cheapest measurement.** On a boot where `systemctl --user is-active
pipewire-pulse.service` says inactive (tonight's does not qualify: it is
running, so Dummy Output catches the app), log `pw-mon` and `pw-metadata -m`
on the A9 (both only watch) from before the blank to after the wake; let the
screen blank on Home and the TV sleep, wake it, and read the app's stream in
`pw-dump` and `pw-top`. Confirmed if the stream is still the start-up one
(same `SDLAudioP` number and serial) with ERR rising 47 a second. The log
then shows the old and new sink ids (equal: candidate 1) and how soon
`default.audio.sink` was set after the new sink appeared (in the same
instant: candidate 2 is possible). A test without the TV, `systemctl --user
restart wireplumber` under the app, changes the console and is MMagTech's
call.

**Fix directions, not chosen or tried:** keep an output present while the
TV sleeps, so SDL always has a default to move to (as pipewire-pulse's
Dummy Output did tonight); have the app reopen its SDL sound when SDL
reports the device removed or the screen wakes; SDL's own fix (#16133,
3.6.0).

### 47. Interface sounds everywhere, and a calmer set, issue #389

**Decided by MMagTech at the TV, 2026-10-14.** The interface sounds are
universal: every screen, panel and menu outside a game makes them (the
game's page, opening a game, Resume, the power menu on Home, the account
switcher, the Library's tabs, the on-screen keyboard, first run joined the
rest). The pause menu, and anything over a game, stays silent. They follow
the Interface sounds level like every other cue.

**No start-up or shut-down sound, ever** (his rule from the project's
start: "one thing I hated about old systems... Sega! It scared the shit out
of me"). Choosing Restart or Power off is silent.

**Restart and Power off fade to black, in silence (#393, MMagTech
2026-10-18: "I would like a fade with no sound if it's not too hard to
implement"; built 2026-10-18).** The curtain (`curtain.cpp`) comes down
over a second (`design::kPowerFade`) over whatever is on screen, the Power
menu and a paused game with it, then the game is left behind the black as
before and logind is asked. The call is made on the clock, not on the
picture, so a frame not drawn delays nothing, and it adds the second and
nothing more. Nothing takes a press meanwhile. A refusal lifts the black and
says it, as before (#241). Sleep does not fade: it comes back, and the
picture would then have to be brought back up on waking. Over an emulator
of its own the console's window is drawn over its frozen picture, so the
fade should cover it, and the emulator is closed behind the black (not yet
seen on the TV); over PCSX2's own window the curtain is one of the things
the console draws over it. After the black the television shows what it
showed before the change: the image's Plymouth reboot or power-off screen
(plymouth-reboot.service ran on the A9's last restart), then the machine
goes off.

**The set is calmer.** The first set (Move 880 Hz over 1320 Hz) read as too
jarring for a quiet, minimal screen. He chose, from samples played in the
chat, a blend halfway between an octave lower and a woody tone (each
partial 2.75 times its pitch); `frontend/src/sound.cpp` keeps the first
set's numbers. One unified set, not sounds per screen. The keyboard uses
the menu Move to go between keys and a 20 ms cut of it to type; a keyboard
with sounds of its own (a wood tap) was tried on the TV and was "too weird
switching".

**Also, Search:** no heading over an empty search while the keys are up
(the bar already says Search; it comes back if the keys are hidden), and
the box says "Search…" instead of "Game name".

### 48. Same-name games, regions and versions, issue #383

**Decided by MMagTech, 2026-10-14; built and judged on the TV the same day**
(the label through the read-only relay's stand-ins, `name:` and `tags:`, on
Home, the Xbox 360 grid and search; `cabinetos-frontend --same-names-test`
checks the wording and every case that must show nothing; the report's list
is `--same-names`, in `samenames.cpp`). Every game keeps its own tile on its
system. No grouping of versions, no picker, no menu, nothing on covers and
nothing on the game's page. **When the selected game shares RomM's `name`
with another game of the same system (RomM's `platform_id`) in the same
list on screen**, the heading shows RomM's
own fields for it, dimmer, after its name: `regions`,
`languages`, `revision`, `tags`. Nothing is added when RomM sends none, so of
two copies the untagged one shows its name alone ("Pokémon Emerald Version"
beside "Pokémon Emerald Version (USA, Europe)"). Nothing is written to the
server. (His two Urban Reigns turned out to be one file added twice, same
SHA-1; he deleted the untagged copy in RomM on 2026-10-14.)

**"Same name, same system, same list", everywhere** (MMagTech,
2026-10-14). Games of different systems never get a label: the system
already tells them apart. A
platform's grid is the whole system, so every twin there gets its label; a
collection, search results, and Home's Recent and Favorites shelves label a
game only when its twin is in that same list (on Home, in the shelf
header). Home asks nothing extra of RomM: what is on it the person played
or chose. **The game's page stays as it is**: each copy has its own saves
(RomM keys them by game), so the wrong copy's page shows no "Saved…" and no
Continue from, but the heading's label is what prevents picking it; not
accounted for unless a player reports it, and the report's list would show it.

**Why not group them** (as RomM's own grouping and Argosy do): it would mean
fewer tiles, but it rests on RomM's sibling grouping, which RomM does not
document (its docs mention it only as the smart collections' `duplicate`
filter, "Games with more than one version") and which a RomM update can
change. MMagTech: "it's going to be a nightmare to maintain over time." On
his library it is also wrong half the time, and its failure hides a game:
Argosy's rule (first metadata ID per system) makes 20 groups there, 10 of
them different games under one tile (Lilo & Stitch with its sequel, Metal
Slug with Metal Slug X, Super Star Wars with The Empire Strikes Back), and
misses all eleven Game & Watch pairs.

**What RomM 5.3.1 sends, checked on his library 2026-10-14:** 29 groups
(60 games) share a name on one platform (by `platform_id`; a first count by
platform slug merged his two arcade platforms). RomM's fields tell most real versions
apart: Jaguar alternates ("1996, a1") and betas ("Beta, 1995"), regions and
revisions (Metroid Prime Hunters "USA", Rev 1). Game & Watch has the most
pairs (screen types) but is excluded on this console, so none of it counts.
They cannot tell apart: a set kept both as a folder and as a zip (Area 51 /
Maximum Force Duo), Bust-A-Move Pocket and Puzzle Bobble Mini, and a game
RomM matched under
another game's name (Lilo & Stitch, Super Mario Advance, Metal Slug, Shock
Troopers, Circus and Clowns, The Lost Vikings, a save state scanned as a
game). Those are fixed in RomM, not on the console.

**Updates and DLC** (#181, when it is built): no choice at all. Every update
and DLC file RomM holds for a game is used. MMagTech: "If you didn't want
your game updated automatically, then you shouldn't have put them in
there." Argosy instead offers a file picker at download with updates and DLC
on by default; not copied.

**But the player is told** (MMagTech, 2026-10-14): the owner put the files
there, but someone else on the same server did not, so the console says the
game has something new, once, in a few words such as "Updated" or "New
content"; not what changed, as modern consoles list it. **Never on the first
play:** a game played for the first time is simply the game as it is. Only
an update or DLC that arrives after someone has played it brings the notice,
for everyone alike, the owner included, since it also confirms to whoever
put the files there that the update reached the game and worked (MMagTech,
2026-10-14). So it shows once the new files are actually in place for the
game, not merely because RomM lists them. Where it shows is settled when
#181 is built. RomM dates every file (`created_at` in each game's `files`).

**RomM's `version` tag:** RomM reads a version from file names (`(v2.00)`)
and stores it, but does not send it. Asked of RomM, rommapp/romm#5243; the
heading adds it only if RomM ships it (nothing of our own meanwhile).

**Each version keeps its own saves**, as RomM keys them, with nothing to
explain since each is its own game.

**The diagnostic report shows it** (MMagTech, 2026-10-14: a player asked for
this and his own library cannot test theirs). A "Same-name games" list beside
the server: per system, every name two or more games share, and per copy the
file name, RomM's `regions`, `languages`, `revision` and `tags` as the console
received them, and the heading the console shows. One report then tells RomM
not reading a tag (in the file name, empty in the field) from the console
showing it wrong (fields right, heading wrong) from a wrong match (two
different files under one name, fixed in RomM). Gathered only when a report
is made, and only for systems this console plays.

**This is the first part of the report that lists games nobody played**
(until now only the games played in the two boots and the emulators' logs
named any). Kept with file names, because without them a tag RomM did not
read cannot be told from one the console showed wrong (MMagTech, 2026-10-14:
"if we think we need to include it to better help troubleshoot ... include
it"). He tells his Discord users it is there; if they push back, it is
discussed again.

### 49. PS Vita (Vita3K), issue #198

**Researched 2026-10-19; decided 2026-10-20: a go, ready to build now that
the 3DS (#524) has merged, by the plan in "Decided, 2026-10-20: the build plan" at the
end of this question, which supersedes the recommendations above it.** The brief
is MMagTech's comment on #198 of the same day: five tests, a failure on any
of the first four a plain no, the fifth his call on the numbers; then which
games are unique, whether touch was play or navigation (Sony's PS TV list as
the pad rule), gyro, controls, start and stop, pin and licence, and the Game
Boy motion games. Read: Vita3K's source at master `7428ca0` (2026-10-19,
numbered build 4202), its compatibility tracker and Xenia Canary's, Sony's
PS TV user's guide, Wikipedia's Vita lists (their PS TV column cites Sony),
No-Intro's Vita DATs (libretro-database `12c21cf`), the pinned mGBA and
Gambatte, SDL 3.4.16, and his RomM read-only with the Mac token. Nothing ran
on the A9 or the VM. The sources, linked, are in the comment on #198.

#### What his server holds

- **26 games, not 27.** The 27th entry, `psvita`, is a folder of 26
  `.psvita` text files (each holds a title ID, ES-DE's launch format) and
  the `vita.py` that wrote them. Not a game.
- **Each game is one zip** (`Dragon's Crown [PCSE00019] [USA] [NoNpDRM].zip`),
  stored without compression, holding only `app/<title ID>/`: `eboot.bin`,
  `sce_sys/param.sfo`, `sce_pfs/`, and the licence
  `sce_sys/package/work.bin` (512 bytes). Read from all 26 central
  directories. No patch or DLC folders; every `param.sfo` says `APP_VER
  01.00`.
- **Every licence is No-Intro's:** each `work.bin`'s SHA-1 matches No-Intro's
  "Sony - PlayStation Vita (PSN)" DAT (2026-10-07) for that USA release.
  There is no Redump Vita DAT: Vita games are cards and downloads, No-Intro's
  domain ("Sony - PlayStation Vita", cards as `.vpk`; "(PSN)", one
  `work.bin` per title).
- **The game files are encrypted** (Sony's PFS layer): the manual pages in
  `sce_sys/manual/` are not readable images in any of the 26. Only
  `param.sfo` and the licence are plain.
- **RomM 5.4.0 leaves `title_id` empty** for all 26; the zip's first 128
  bytes name it (`app/PCSE00655/`).
- **No Vita firmware** on the server (`/api/firmware?platform_id=29` is
  empty).

#### The five tests

| Test | Answer | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1. What it needs from RomM | **passes, once he uploads two firmware files** | A game is one zip with its licence inside. Firmware: Sony's system software and its font package, which Sony names `PSP2UPDAT.PUP` alike, so they need two names in RomM's Vita `bios/` folder. Vita3K installs each without a window (`--firmware`, one per run, `main.cpp:139-145`), as RPCS3's `--installfw` installs `PS3UPDAT*.PUP` (`standalone_rpcs3.cpp`). Vita3K's quickstart makes both step 3 of 5; it decrypts games without them, but system modules and fonts come from them |
| 2. No user interaction | **passes on paper** | `--frontend sdl` (b852ad972, 2026-10-09): "a plain window that runs the app given by -r and quits with it". That frontend shows no dialog; the welcome, the update check and the compatibility download belong to the Qt window. User `00` is made by itself. To set: `discord-rich-presence: false` (on by default), `http-enable: false` (games may use HTTP by default), `show-compile-shaders: false`, a log level. Traps: `-F` does nothing there and the window opens at 960x544, so gamescope must fill the screen; `-r` checks the title against the default config's `pref-path` before `-c` is read, so the console writes Vita3K's own `config.yml` before each start, as it deletes Edge's |
| 3. The cache model | **passes, the way PS3 packages do** | A Vita game is installed before it runs: Vita3K extracts the zip, then decrypts it with `work.bin`, deleting the copy if that fails (`interface.cpp:96-111, 190-252`). So the cached thing is the installed folder, made once on the download worker in the game's folder and removed with it, as PS3 packages are (`standalone_rpcs3.cpp:1-46`); the zip goes after. Costs: about twice the game's size on disk during the install (Killzone: Mercenary is 3.2 GB); install time unmeasured. Installing from a path reinstalls every time (`interface.cpp:196-204`), so starts use `-r`. Outside the folder: the shader and pipeline cache (`~/.cache/Vita3K/shaders/<ID>`), console-wide as Xenia's is |
| 4. Saves | **passes** | One folder per game, `ux0/user/00/savedata/<dir>`, zipped and sent as PSP's and Xbox 360's are, kept in the person's folder as Xenia's content root is. Vita3K has no save states at all. A real Vita's saves are sealed to that Vita and will not load, as a real 360's do not |
| 5. Playability | **his call; on the labels, not more experimental than Xbox 360** | below |

**Playability, counted 2026-10-19** (open reports per label):

| | Playable to the end | Reaches play | Reports |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vita3K (Vita3K/compatibility) | 1,900 (56.9%) | 2,834 (84.9%): Playable, "Ingame +" 532, "Ingame -" 402 | 3,340 |
| Xenia Canary (xenia-canary/game-compatibility) | 289 (25.8%) | 1,056 (94.4%): playable, "gameplay" 767 | 1,119 |

The scales differ: Xenia's "gameplay" is any working gameplay, Vita3K
splits it in two. Both are players' reports on any hardware, some years
old, and the console runs Edge, not Canary. **His 26:** 23 Playable;
Killzone: Mercenary "Menu" (Vita3K/compatibility#278), MotorStorm RC
"Intro" (#3112, Windows, build 3725), Skullgirls 2nd Encore "Intro" (#4039,
Linux on a Radeon RX 6600, build 4058, 2026-06: a grey screen after the
logo). His eight Xbox 360 games for comparison: five labelled playable (both
Forzas, both Gears, Left 4 Dead 2), three unlisted, all eight played on the
A9 (question 34).

#### Touch: Sony's PS TV list is a pad rule with a pointer

Sony's PS TV user's guide, "Using the touch pointer": in the games Sony
allowed, a controller does touch through a pointer. L3 shows it for the
screen, R3 for the rear touch pad, both together for both; the left stick
(or a DUALSHOCK 4's touch pad) moves it and L2 taps; the right stick brings a
second pointer, tapped with R2. So a game on Sony's list may still need a
tap: Sony judged it playable with the pointer. Wikipedia's Vita lists carry
Sony's list as a PS TV column, sourced to Sony Japan's software search and
the US store's "PS Vita Games (for PS TV)": 1,075 Yes, 569 No, 16 Partial of
1,664 rows. By name, not title ID: Sony's full list lived in a PS Store
category (`STORE-MSF77008-PSTVCOMPATIBLE`), and no copy keyed by title ID
was found.

**What reaches Vita3K today: no touch at all.** Every emulator of its own
gets the console's virtual pads, which carry neither a touch pad nor motion
(`vpad.h`); SDL 3.4.16's Linux joystick code has no touch pad support for
such a device (`SDL_sysjoystick.c`). Vita3K takes a real DUALSHOCK 4 or
DualSense touch pad as the front screen (`touch.cpp:251-290`); only its Qt
window switches it to the rear pad, and no frontend has a stick pointer. The PS TV pointer is an open request upstream,
Vita3K/Vita3K#3707 ("PSTV 'touch pointer' function", 2025-12-22, no reply).
**So Sony's list can be the one rule only once Vita3K has the pointer;**
without it, a listed game that needs a tap stops at that tap.

  needed (or none found) all play here already, on PS3, Switch, Wii U, Wii or Xbox 360, most
  as the same game. The four listed games that need a tap are Guacamelee!
  (also here) and three unique ones: Killzone: Mercenary, Table Top Racing
  and TxK. Killzone was made ready for the PS TV by update 1.11 ("reworked
  all the touch mechanics", PlayStation Blog, 2014-10-13); his copy is 1.00,
  and updates wait on #181 ("Updates and DLC as separate files in RomM
  (Switch, PS3, Xbox 360)").
- **So without a pointer, the Vita adds no game to his library that does
  not already play here; with it, two (three once updates come).** The other
  five unique games are off Sony's list: four need touch, and WipEout 2048
  is off it although its touch and tilt are optional.

#### Gyro

- **His 26:** motion is required only in Gravity Rush (the Gravity Slide)
  and Mutant Blobs Attack (one bonus level); both are off Sony's list and
  need touch anyway. Optional in Killzone, Ninja Gaiden Sigma Plus, Banana
  Splitz and WipEout 2048; unclear in TxK. **A gyro would unlock none of
  his games.**
- **Across the Vita:** no public list of games that need motion was found.
  Vita3K's tracker has 4 open reports labelled "motion missing" and 2
  "sensor missing".
- **A Wii-style greying rule needs data,** as GameTDB is for Wii; nothing
  says which Vita games need motion, so "needs motion" could not be told
  from "needs touch". Sony's list leaves the motion games out already:
  the PS TV had no gyroscope for Vita games at all (Wikipedia's PS TV
  article, citing Sony's 2013 announcement), so every listed game plays
  without motion.
- **Could a DualSense unlock them?** Vita3K takes motion from any SDL pad
  reporting both sensors (`ctrl.cpp:102-108`, Vita3K PR #2628, 2023-09-02),
  and a DualSense does. But the virtual pads carry none, and SDL 3.4.16 pairs
  a pad with its motion device by matching their UNIQ strings
  (`SDL_sysjoystick.c:1530-1584`), which uinput cannot set (no such ioctl in
  `uinput.h`): one player at best, unproven. The other way, handing Vita3K
  the real pads, is open because Vita3K's SDL is 3.4.16 as the console's is,
  so the numbering fault `vpad.h` guards against does not arise; it would
  give up the console's player order and the pause menu's hold on the pads,
  for one system.
- **Recommended: no gyro for the Vita.** It unlocks nothing on his library,
  there is no data to grey by, and it is a second input path.

#### The Game Boy motion games

- **mGBA at the pin** (`e31759b`) asks for libretro's sensor interface
  (`RETRO_ENVIRONMENT_GET_SENSOR_INTERFACE`, `libretro.c:1089-1114`) and
  feeds the accelerometer's X and Y to tilt carts and the gyroscope's Z to
  gyro carts (`:2552-2565`). Its own table marks them: WarioWare: Twisted!
  (`RZWE`, gyro and rumble), Yoshi Topsy-Turvy (`KYGE`, tilt), and Japan's
  Korokoro Puzzle (`KHPJ`, tilt) (`src/gba/overrides.c`). The console's core
  host never answers that call (question 35: "the frontend does not offer it
  yet"), and mGBA has no stick stand-in, so these games get no motion.
- **Gambatte at the pin** (`d9d6cd0`) refuses MBC7 carts ("MBC7 ROM not
  supported", `cartridge.cpp:905`). His Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble is cart type
  0x22, MBC7 (read from his file), so it does not start at all today. mGBA's
  Game Boy core runs MBC7 from the same motion source (`src/gb/mbc.c`).
- **His server has two:** WarioWare: Twisted! (its header says `RZWE`) and
  Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble.
- **3DS:** there is no 3DS core on the console. Azahar's libretro core
  (master `987f184`, 2026-10-17) takes gyro and accelerometer through the
  same interface (`src/citra_libretro/input/input_factory.cpp:99-125`).
- **So one piece serves the cores** (answer the sensor interface from the
  player's own pad, in process, where the console already reads the real
  pads), **but not Vita3K**, a separate program behind virtual pads: two
  pieces, not one. A greying rule by cart hardware is possible from data
  (mGBA's table for GBA; header byte 0x147 = 0x22 for Game Boy), and Kirby
  would also need MBC7 carts sent to mGBA, a choice of core by cart type. If
  any motion is built, this is the cheapest; whether it is wanted is his
  call.

#### Controls, start and stop, pin and licence (for when it is built)

- **Controls:** the Vita has L and R only, no stick clicks. Vita3K gives L2,
  R2, L3 and R3 only to games that ask for the PS TV's extended pad
  (`ctrl.cpp:199-219`). With `pstv-mode` each pad is its own port and the
  game sees a PS TV; without it every pad is merged into port 1 and ports
  above answer "no device" (`ctrl.cpp:263-287`). So two players need
  `pstv-mode`, which is also Sony's convention for the listed games.
- **Start and stop:** silent start as in test 2. A failed load logs an error
  and exits -1 (255 to the shell); an unknown `-r` exits 4. SIGTERM becomes
  SDL's quit event, which the SDL frontend handles like a window close
  (`session.cpp:295-296`), stopping the session and exiting; a game's own
  exit ends Vita3K with the game's code (`:374-375`). Batocera's patch says
  stopping "can hang" on guest threads, so a kill after a wait, as for the
  others. The log is `~/.cache/Vita3K/vita3k.log`, emptied at each start,
  TRACE by default. Whether a save written just before a close survives is
  for the hand test.
- **Pin and licence:** GPL-2.0. Upstream's own release is a moving
  `continuous`, but every master build is also a numbered release in
  Vita3K/Vita3K-builds (4202 is `7428ca0`, 2026-10-19) with an x86-64
  AppImage: pinned by tag and checksum, built into the image as Xenia's
  AppImage is, fetched from GitHub at build time only. 92 numbered builds in
  the last 90 days. The SDL frontend is ten days old.

#### The A9 hand test (step 3 of #198), when he names a time (superseded 2026-10-20 by the plan's hand test, below)

Needs: the A9 free and him at the TV; the two Sony firmware files on RomM
(his upload, a write to his server); a numbered Vita3K build run by hand in
a scratch folder, as `~/x360/t360.sh` was; his DualSense only if the touch
pad is still wanted. To see: both firmware files install without a window;
three installs, with time and peak disk (Killzone the largest); `--frontend
sdl -r <ID>` starting with no dialog and the picture filling the TV; frames
(frames.py) in one 2D and one 3D game (Shovel Knight; WipEout 2048 or Gravity
Rush) at 1x and 2x resolution; Killzone and Skullgirls, to see whether their
labels hold here; a close by SIGTERM (time, exit code) and a save made just
before it; two pads with `pstv-mode` in Skullgirls; a game's own exit.

#### Recommendation, 2026-10-19 (not decided; superseded 2026-10-20, below)

**No, for now.** None of the first four tests fails, and on the labels
Vita3K is no further from finished than Xbox 360. But Sony's own pad rule
assumes the PS TV's touch pointer, which Vita3K lacks; without it Sony's
list over-promises on the games that need a tap, and the only honest rule
left is a judgement per game, which the project does not make. On his
library the Vita adds nothing that does not already play here unless the
pointer comes, and then two games. **It becomes a go with conditions** when
(1) Vita3K ships the pointer (upstream first, on his go: support for
Vita3K/Vita3K#3707), (2) Sony's list is in hand by title ID to ship as data,
and (3) the hand test passes. **No gyro for the Vita** in any case. Game Boy
motion is a separate, smaller question for him.

**His question:** "how vital is that pointer to playing games? On DS we use
the right thumbstick for the pointer. I also discussed the PS5 touchpad. Can
you research if anybody else does this type of implementation? Or is this
emulator pretty much only used on phones and devices that already have touch
support?" Research only, nothing ran on the A9. Read: Vita3K master

site; Vita3K/Vita3K-builds and Vita3K/Vita3K-Android releases (GitHub API,
2026-10-19); Batocera `7fa4f7c` (2026-10-20), EmuDeck `dddb302`
(2026-10-05), RetroDECK `7786a84` (2026-10-03); gamescope master `4d5b7f3`
(2026-10-19); SDL 3.4.16 (`fa2c02b`, Vita3K's own submodule); Wikipedia's
